t: For necessary expenses in carrying out provisions of title 23, United States Code, to be derived from the Highway Trust Fund and to remain available until expended, $9,000,000.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation of Highway Trust Fund money for carrying out title 23. One might suppose that title 23 highway programs involve coordination with states, but the section itself names no outside party and sets up no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No one outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision here.
fable.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out provisions of title 23, United States Code, to be derived from the Highway Trust Fund and to remain available until expended, $9,000,000.

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations clause that authorizes the expenditure of funds for specific statutory purposes. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a decision is made. It merely provides the financial resources to carry out existing laws.
qwen_block.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out provisions of title 23, United States Code, to be derived from the Highway Trust Fund and to remain available until expended, $9,000,000.

opus.w: This section only appropriates $9,000,000 from the Highway Trust Fund for expenses under title 23. It does not involve any party outside the federal government in a federal decision. The general reference to title 23 does not bring that title's procedures into this section, so like Example 1, it is just a funding provision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation clause that authorizes a specific amount of funding ($9,000,000) from the Highway Trust Fund to carry out provisions of Title 23. It does not establish any advisory committees, require public comment periods, mandate consultation with outside entities, or grant rights to sue. It merely provides financial resources for existing statutory programs. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: For necessary expenses in carrying out provisions of title 23, United States Code, to be derived from the Highway Trust Fund and to remain available until expended, $9,000,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "carrying out provisions of title 23" implicitly involves participation because Title 23 contains many provisions about public hearings and consultation. However, this specific section is merely an appropriation clause authorizing funds. It does not itself mandate or describe any participatory process; it simply provides the money to execute existing laws. The definition requires the section itself to involve participation (e.g., requiring a comment period, establishing an advisory board with outside members, etc.). An appropriation bill section that just lists a dollar amount for a general purpose does not meet the threshold for "participation" unless it explicitly ties the funding to a specific participatory mechanism or creates a new one. Here, it is just a budget authorization.
